The argument that the “Ravens tried multiple times to extend Likely” is frustrating to me when you consider the context. 

Of course this is all conjecture since we’re not in the room when these talks happen but here is my read on the situation based on things I heard throughout, context clues, and reports.

• They were close to an extension last offseason early in camp then he hurt his foot and they paused negotiations. 

• When negotiations resumed the injury was used as a reason not to offer him as much as he wanted. 

• His role in the offense was reduced due to missed time from the injury and that was used against him in negotiations. 

• They then tried to offer him similar money to a 30-year old Mark Andrews and when Likely said no they extended Andrews. 

• The Ravens weren’t aggressive in trying to keep Likely because they negotiated with him with the comfort of knowing they had Andrews in their back pocket.

• The Ravens tried to save a few million by moneyballing the TE position with a player we all knew was past his prime. They did what was safe instead of offering Likely what he deserved.

Summary: Extended Andrews out of comfort and emotion for what he’s done and not what he was going to do and lowballed Likely for what he had done and not what we knew he would do
